final_answer:
Let
\[
r=\max(n-q,0).
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Gal}(K_{n,q}/\mathbb Q)\cong C_{2^r}\rtimes (\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times,}
\]
where \(C_{2^r}\) is trivial when \(r=0\), and \(u\in(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times\) acts on \(C_{2^r}\cong\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z\) by multiplication by \(u\bmod 2^r\).

Equivalently:
\[
\operatorname{Gal}(K_{n,q}/\mathbb Q)\cong
\begin{cases}
(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times, & q\ge n,\\[2mm]
C_{2^{n-q}}\rtimes(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times, & q<n.
\end{cases}
\]

Proof. Use the identity
\[
f(z+z^{-1})=z^2+z^{-2},
\]
so by induction
\[
f^{\circ m}(z+z^{-1})=z^{2^m}+z^{-2^m}.
\]
Put
\[
L=\ell^{2^q}.
\]
The equation
\[
f^{\circ n}(x)=L+L^{-1}
\]
has roots
\[
x_j=\rho\zeta^j+\rho^{-1}\zeta^{-j},\qquad j\in\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z,
\]
where \(\zeta=\zeta_{2^n}\), and \(\rho\) is chosen so that
\[
\rho^{2^n}=L.
\]
Thus, if \(q<n\), take \(\rho=\ell^{1/2^{n-q}}\); if \(q\ge n\), take \(\rho=\ell^{2^{q-n}}\in\mathbb Q\).

When \(q\ge n\), all roots lie in \(\mathbb Q(\zeta_{2^n})\), and the roots \(x_j\) generate \(\zeta_{2^n}\), since \(\rho\ne \rho^{-1}\). Hence
\[
K_{n,q}=\mathbb Q(\zeta_{2^n}),
\]
so
\[
\operatorname{Gal}(K_{n,q}/\mathbb Q)\cong(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times.
\]

Now suppose \(q<n\), and set \(r=n-q\). Then \(\rho^{2^r}=\ell\), and
\[
K_{n,q}\subseteq M:=\mathbb Q(\rho,\zeta_{2^n}).
\]
The field \(M\) is Galois over \(\mathbb Q\): it is the splitting field of
\[
(X^{2^r}-\ell)\Phi_{2^n}(X).
\]
Since \(\mathbb Q(\zeta_{2^n})\) is ramified only at \(2\), while every nontrivial subfield of \(\mathbb Q(\rho)\) is ramified at the odd prime \(\ell\), the two fields intersect trivially. Hence
\[
[M:\mathbb Q]=2^r\varphi(2^n).
\]

Every automorphism of \(M\) has the form
\[
\sigma_{v,u}(\rho)=\zeta^{2^qv}\rho,\qquad
\sigma_{v,u}(\zeta)=\zeta^u,
\]
with
\[
v\in\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z,\qquad u\in(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times.
\]
It acts on the roots by
\[
\sigma_{v,u}(x_j)
=\rho\zeta^{uj+2^qv}+\rho^{-1}\zeta^{-uj-2^qv}
=x_{uj+2^qv}.
\]
Thus \(M\) preserves the splitting field \(K_{n,q}\).

This action is faithful: if \(\sigma_{v,u}\) fixes every \(x_j\), then
\[
x_{uj+2^qv}=x_j
\]
for all \(j\). The roots \(x_j\) are distinct, because \(x_a=x_b\) would imply either \(\zeta^a=\zeta^b\), or else \(\rho^2\) is a root of unity, impossible since \(\rho>1\). Therefore
\[
uj+2^qv\equiv j\pmod{2^n}
\]
for every \(j\), forcing \(u\equiv1\pmod{2^n}\) and \(v\equiv0\pmod{2^r}\). Hence the restriction map
\[
\operatorname{Gal}(M/\mathbb Q)\to\operatorname{Gal}(K_{n,q}/\mathbb Q)
\]
is injective. Since \(K_{n,q}\subseteq M\), this forces \(K_{n,q}=M\).

The group law is
\[
(v,u)(v',u')=(v+uv',uu'),
\]
with \(v\) taken modulo \(2^r\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Gal}(K_{n,q}/\mathbb Q)\cong
C_{2^r}\rtimes(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times,
\]
as claimed.
